items.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued September 22 at 4:00AM EDT until September 26 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along the beaches of the Outer Banks, especially
on Hatteras and Ocraoke Island.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Friday evening. Most
significant impacts expected during the Thursday evening and
Friday morning high tide cycles.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding may
extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and
businesses. Some roads and low lying property including parking
lots, parks, lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will
experience shallow flooding. Vulnerable areas along Highway 12
on Ocracoke and Hatteras Island are especially at risk for
inundation from the oceanside.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued September 22 at 5:46AM EDT until September 25 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and
seas 14 to 19 ft expected.

* WHERE...The coastal waters from Duck to Cape Hatteras, and the
offshore waters from Duck to Cape Hatteras.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Wednesday to 6 PM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
